messages:
support: Heads-up — getting three separate customer escalations about 5xx/errors on hosted API since ~09:12 UTC. Spike on 5xx rate, timeouts reported, particularly for long-streaming chat requests. Sample customer ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/12345
eng-oncall: Acknowledged. Are these correlated with the 09:10 rollout? cc @eng-runtime @eng-infra
deploy-bot: deploy finished: rollout-id=roll-2026-03-17-0910, sha=ba7c1f, scope=staged-20%, config: batch_max_tokens=1024 -> 512, kv_cache_enabled=true -> false (experiment), route_tag=stable->v2prefix
eng-runtime: I see a big jump in request queue length on the serving tier at 09:11:30 UTC. Latency P95 for token generation went from 180ms -> 1.8s, followed by 502s from gateway. Suspect the kv_cache flip — disabling prefix/KV caching will increase KV fetches and memory pressure on nodes.
support-engineer: Pasted sample gateway log from customer: ```[09:12:48] gateway: upstream error status=502, downstream timeout 60000ms, req_id=abc-123
[09:12:49] serving: connection closed: kv::fetch timeout 250ms, model=redwood-7b, seq_len=1024
```
eng-infra: Confirmed nodes serving the canary saw elevated OOM_kill and PG cache misses. Also saw a higher number of short-lived connections stacking up on proxy. We should consider traffic shift back while we investigate config.
eng-sre: Starting coordinated rollback to previous config (rollout-id=roll-2026-03-17-0910 -> rollback target roll-2026-03-10-0800). Will reduce staged traffic to 0% over next 3 minutes then promote previous. ETA ~6 minutes. Initiating now.
product-manager: Notifying affected customers in status page + support triage. ETA for message 10m. Please post a short blurb once we have confirmation the rollback is complete.
eng-runtime: To verify: run `redwoodctl admin metrics --service serving --filter rollout=roll-2026-03-17-0910` and check `kv_cache_misses_total` and `inflight_requests`. Also check shedder logs: `/var/log/shedder.log` for recent entries. If KV cache disabled, we should see kv_cache_misses spike.
eng-infra: Running healthcheck sweep and will tail proxy metrics: `kubectl -n inference logs -l app=ingress-proxy --tail=200` — I see repeated `upstream error: context deadline exceeded` lines.
eng-sre: Rollback command issued: `redwoodctl rollout rollback roll-2026-03-17-0910 --to roll-2026-03-10-0800 --now`. Traffic shifting... 20% -> 10% -> 0% (2m)
eng-oncall: Watching real-user metrics: 5xx rate dropping from 6.2% -> 1.1% after traffic at 0% for canary. Latency P95 improving. Can someone confirm gateway 502s gone for the affected tenants?
support: Support ops seeing customer ticket statuses update to "recovering". One large customer reported timeouts resolved. Will mark incident ongoing->recovering.
eng-ml: Confirming model infra wasn't changed. This looks purely ingress/config related, not model runtime changes. Quantization/weights unchanged.
product-manager: Posted status: "Investigating increased 5xx errors after a staged config change. Rollback in progress. We will update in 15 minutes." :hourglass_flowing_sand:
eng-infra: Post-rollback sanity checks: memory pressure back to baseline, KV miss rate normalized, no new OOMs. Proxy connection backlog cleared.
eng-sre: Rollback complete and verified at 09:20:12 UTC. Traffic fully on previous rollout. Will keep monitoring for 30m.
eng-oncall: Confirmed last_message_ts 1809999150 — system metrics stable, error rate back to normal baseline. Closing active mitigation.
support-engineer: Leaving notes for follow-up with customer ops: check any billing anomalies for requests that errored, offer credits case-by-case. Ticket owners notified.
eng-runtime: Action items: 1) Revert the experiment flag change from `kv_cache_enabled=false` to an opt-in behind a strict canary with smaller batch limits. 2) Add automated canary health gating on kv_cache_misses and OOM rates. 3) Postmortem runbook entry. Assigning to @eng-runtime for follow-up.
product-manager: Filing postmortem and owners. Will draft customer-facing summary after engineering writeup. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
customer-ops-bot: Noted affected accounts, creating follow-ups for billing and outreach.
eng-sre: We'll schedule a brief blameless postmortem and include steps for safer config flips (feature flags + automated metric gates).
